description: Compute the cheapest Minecraft anvil combine path to migrate an item's existing enchantments (and prior-work penalty count) to a target enchantment set. sourceItem and targetItem must be the same item id (e.g. both 'diamond_sword') — a mismatch is a tool error, not a silent conversion. Inventory usage is set by two optional inputs: with no availableSources the inventory is not used ("Don't use": every needed book/item is assumed obtainable); with availableSources the plan may use them when they help and assumes the rest is obtainable ("May use"); with inventoryOnly: true, which is never implied, only the listed items are considered, lower levels may be combined into higher ones (two same-level books into the next level) but no outside book is ever assumed ("Only use"; a plan the inventory cannot complete comes back as error 'blocked_plan'). Optional `objective`: 'min_xp' (default, fewest XP levels) or 'min_prior_work' (fewest anvil operations on the finished item so it stays cheap to upgrade later, then fewest XP levels); when set, the response also reports the objective used, the total XP and the result's prior-work count. Returns ordered combine steps, per-step and total cost, feasibility, and a plain-language summary. Fails clearly, as a tool error, if the target requires downgrading an enchantment level (not possible on a vanilla anvil).

availableSources.description: The books/items the player already owns, i.e. the inventory. Omit it or pass [] for "Don't use": no inventory is provided, so the plan assumes every needed book/item is obtainable (a fresh single-enchantment book for each target enchantment). Pass one or more sources for "May use": the plan picks those that make it cheaper, ignores the ones that don't help, and still assumes anything the sources cannot provide is obtainable. Passing sources never implies "Only use"; that needs inventoryOnly: true.

cured.description: Only meaningful when villagerTrade is true: whether that specific villager has been cured, for the discounted emerald price in the plan's emerald-cost estimate. Never affects XP level cost.

enchantments.description: Enchantments already present on this source

level.description: Enchantment level (Roman-numeral level as an integer)

isBook.description: True if this source is an enchanted book rather than an item

itemId.description: Item id this source is, e.g. 'diamond_pickaxe' — required when isBook is false

origin.description: Informational only — where this source came from

priorWorkCount.description: This source's own 'too expensive' prior-work counter, if it has already been anvil-combined before (0 for a fresh book/item)

quantity.description: How many independent physical copies of this exact source are owned (default 1). Ignored when unlimited is true.

sourceId.description: Caller-chosen id used to reference this source in the plan output

unlimited.description: True if more of this exact source can always be obtained on demand (e.g. a standing villager trade) — treated as reusable without limit instead of a fixed quantity.

villagerTrade.description: True if this source is a STANDING, repeatable villager trade (not a specific physical copy you already own) — this, not origin, is what makes a source cost emeralds in the plan's emerald-cost estimate. A source you physically own, even one whose origin happens to be tagged 'villager_trade' as a flavor note on how you got it, should leave this false/unset and stays free. Never affects XP level cost.

inventoryOnly.description: "Only use": only if you set this to true (it is never implied, not even when availableSources is non-empty). The plan then considers only the items in availableSources (respecting each one's quantity/unlimited) and never assumes an outside book is obtainable. It may still start by combining lower levels into higher ones, for example two same-level books into the next level. If the inventory cannot reach the target, the result is feasible: false with error 'blocked_plan' (the cheapest plan assuming each missing book, with blockers). Omit it or pass false for the default ("Don't use" with no sources, "May use" with sources).

objective.description: What to optimise. 'min_xp' (default) finds the plan with the fewest total XP levels. 'min_prior_work' finds the plan whose FINISHED item has the lowest prior-work count (fewest anvil operations on it, so it stays cheap to upgrade again later — each extra operation doubles the prior-work penalty of any future combine), and among plans with that count picks the cheapest in XP. 'min_prior_work' may cost more XP; when this parameter is given the response also reports the objective used, the total XP and the result's prior-work count so the two modes can be compared. Omit for the original min_xp behaviour and response.

level.description: Enchantment level (Roman-numeral level as an integer)

id.description: Item id, e.g. 'diamond_sword' — must match targetItem.id

material.description: Optional material override for the item, if applicable

name.description: The item's existing custom name, if any

priorWorkCount.description: The item's existing 'too expensive' prior-work-penalty counter, if known

level.description: Enchantment level (Roman-numeral level as an integer)

id.description: Item id, e.g. 'diamond_sword' — must match sourceItem.id, or the tool returns an error

name.description: Desired custom name. A rename is included only if this differs from sourceItem.name (use '' here to clear an existing name) — cost is a flat +1 XP level, the actual text has no effect on cost. Omit to leave the name untouched.

version.description: Game version, e.g. '1.21.4'; defaults to the latest supported version for the chosen edition
